text:
maya: FYI — after merging the lattice-batcher change I'm seeing a repeating p95 oscillation on short sequences in canary. It looks like decode path latency moves up/down in a ~30s pattern.
jon: can you paste the mini profile? shortseq-only or broad?
maya: shortseq heavy (<=32). quick sample from the CPU timeline on canary:
```
canary host: decode p95: 29ms -> 64ms -> 31ms -> 67ms (30s period)
flame: dispatch_queue wait spikes aligned with kv-evict path
batcher: threshold toggles between 8 and 32 concurrent batches
KV cache hits stable
```
aisha: hmm that threshold toggling smells like the new sampler heuristic from PR 4698 — it may be collapsing batches briefly then reopening, causing kernel switch thrash. I flagged that PR last week as risky for shortseq.
li: starting a bisect run now across canary commits. I'll run a narrow commit-range bisect to find the exact merge. ETA ~10m.
samir: if li finds a culprit we should either hotfix revert or pin the old batcher heuristic for the canary cohort. This is a rollout blocker for the release tomorrow.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy halted: hold=true reason="p95 oscillation observed" trigger=maya
li: bisect result: culprit narrowed to commit 0d4f8b2 — sampler: adaptive-threshold change (PR 4698). Reproduced locally with small harness.
jon: nice, can you include the minimal repro harness and exact config differences? We need to see why it flips. Also check kernel selection logs to see if we flip attention kernel variants during oscillation.
maya: repro harness and logs: https://internal/redwood/perf/1723456789-flip-repro
snippet of interesting logs:
```
2024-03-12T12:01:10Z batcher: threshold=8 active=12 -> overflow
2024-03-12T12:01:11Z sampler: heuristic=adaptive threshold->32
2024-03-12T12:01:11Z kernel-selector: switching attn_kernel=fast32 -> attn_kernel=fallback16
2024-03-12T12:01:41Z sampler: adaptive threshold->8
```
ci-bot: perf canary tests: shortseq-decode p95 regression +42% between commit 0d4f8b2 and previous. Full CI perf suite flagged (see job 88432).
samir: given the morning release, propose: revert the adaptive-threshold change in canary, open a follow-up to rework heuristic with hysteresis. I'll draft the revert PR.
aisha: +1 on hysteresis. The rapid flip means there's no hysteresis and kernel selection thrashes. Maybe keep threshold deltas gated by a time window and require stable load for 2 windows before changing.
li: reverting on canary now (rolling back to prior sampler binary). Monitoring.
deploy-bot: canary-rollback started by samir — revert PR 4701
maya: thanks — after rollback p95 looks stable at ~30ms for shortseq. I'll keep the harness running for 1hr and report if anything else shows.
samir: follow-ups: (1) add unit test for sampler hysteresis, (2) add kernel-selection telemetry to surface rapid kernel flips, (3) run soak on small seqs for 24h before re-landing.
jon: will help with telemetry dashboard. we should also add a perf CI check that compares shortseq p95 delta for canary commits.
maya: agreed. Thanks team :thumbsup!
